validation.notes: Repaired the shared cwd-encoding contract between the legacy session producer (packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts:112) and the session reader's canonical lookup (packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts:592). Both now use `--${cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`, which sanitizes slash, backslash and drive colon; migrations.ts previously missed backslash and session-manager.ts previously missed colon, so migrated files landed in a directory the reader never inspected. .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads both real submitted modules via .prale-eval/subject.mjs (only getAgentDir and a deterministic readdirSync ordering are faked) and, for absolute POSIX cwds containing slash, backslash, colon, spaces and non-ASCII text, asserts: migration moves the legacy .jsonl into exactly getDefaultSessionDir(cwd, agentDir); loadEntriesFromFile/ SessionManager.open/ continueRecent/ findById/ list/ findMostRecentSession all resolve that file with identical bytes, Unicode and entry order; a malformed JSONL line is skipped without reordering later entries; a pre-existing target is not overwritten and the colliding source stays in place; malformed-header, cwd-less and non-.jsonl files are untouched; and repeated migration runs change nothing. Detection was verified by restoring each faulty baseline alone: faulty session-manager.ts produced 'AssertionError: reader canonical dir must encode slash, backslash and colon ...' and faulty migrations.ts produced 'AssertionError: migrated session file lands in the reader's dir ...', both plain node:assert/strict failures (no crash/import error/timeout), after which the fixed state was restored and the script passed. Stages are chained with promises; no timers, randomness, network or real clock ordering are used. The script creates its inputs under .prale-eval/.tmp-regression and removes them in a finally block. Limitation: the workspace has no node_modules, so the repository's vitest/tsc toolchain could not be executed; Node 24 running the regression script is the validation of record.

claims.claim: Legacy migration and the session manager must share one observable cwd-to-session-directory encoding for absolute POSIX cwds containing slash, backslash and colon.
Migrated sessions are readable through the real reader with Unicode, entry order and bytes preserved; malformed lines are skipped.
Collisions never overwrite data and repeated migration is safe.
